raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Reopened from #40742. GitHub closed that PR on 2 October when the fork it came from was deleted; its review history is still there.

## Motivation

Long-prefix Triton attention is the main prefill cost for MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. In a six-step late-prefill profile, the nine global-attention layers consumed 13,124 ms per rank, versus 102 ms for the 39 sliding-window layers.

## Modifications

Use a 128-row query tile and 128-row prefix tile for the measured RTX PRO 6000 shape: BF16 current Q/K/V, E4M3 FP8 cached K/V, QK192/V128, 32 query heads, two KV heads, page size one, at least 512 queries and every prefix at least 8,192 tokens. The current-token tile remains unchanged.

Pass the existing CPU prefix lengths through an optional trailing argument. Short prefixes, other devices or geometries, custom masks, window/sink attention and CUDA graph capture retain the original dispatch. Captured graphs can replay with different device prefix lengths, so capture deliberately retains the original partition.

## Accuracy Tests

- Sixteen real-GPU regression cases passed on each of the two cards, including ragged prefixes, exact fallback comparisons and CUDA graph replay from an 8,192-token prefix to a 257-token prefix.
- The isolated 524K-prefix configuration screen measured relative RMS difference 0.001762 and maximum absolute difference 0.0000611 against the original partition.
- A matched whole-model likelihood check used 64 fixed 16K contexts, 1,024 scored suffix tokens each, with the same FP8 KV and 4K prefill chunk on both runtimes. NLL was 1.9191643658 before and 1.9151446877 after; all 65,536 scored positions were finite and the cached prefix was verified for every case. This measures numerical agreement, not byte identity.
- Full-model validation used the public `tiyuvta/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-NVFP4` artifact at `58edbd0c60ace653512b8f423bf41813331ef9e3`, plus the loader fixes proposed separately in #42450 and #42452.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, a 2,048-query / 524,288-prefix isolated attention call measured 184.636 ms with M64/N64 and 91.568 ms with M128/prefix-N128 (eight warps, one stage; five timed calls after warm-up). The latter uses 90,112 shared bytes under the device's 101,376-byte limit.

A complete 786,034-token cold request with the optimized runtime produced its first token in 291.394 s and correctly retrieved three planted values. The earlier runtime required 536.462 s. This complete-runtime comparison also increases the prefill chunk from 2,048 to 4,096, so it is not an isolated attribution to this patch. Both runs used TP2/EP2, FP8 KV, host caching and the vendor's sampled defaults.

The qualification image pins upstream `0f6761b54facebb47f2068f87ecccd8f14da3a0e`, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and FlashInfer 0.6.18. No result is claimed for another GPU family.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed Python files pass isort, Ruff and codespell; the private integration's hosted lint passed.
- [x] Added registered GPU regression tests in the kernel unit suite.
- [x] Documented the dispatch boundary in the function docstring and tests.
- [x] Provided accuracy and speed results with their scope.
- [x] Kept the change additive and preserved positional-call compatibility.

Duplicate preflight, 2026-09-22: the three-file patch applies cleanly to current upstream main; no overlapping open or recently closed PR was found.

## Rebase validation (2026-10-02)

Rebased onto upstream `f2385314b2b3` on 2026-10-04; the commit is patch-identical to the 2026-10-02 revision, and upstream has not touched the three changed files since. The repo's pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files. The registered regression suite needs an SM120 GPU (it skips on CPU) and was not rerun.

Changed Python files pass isort, Ruff lint/format and codespell; the diff passes whitespace checks. Earlier hardware and whole-model measurements above predate this rebase and were not rerun. Upstream test workflows still require a maintainer to add `run-ci`.

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import sglang.kernels.ops.attention.extend_attention as attention
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=40, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not attention._is_rtx_pro_6000,
+    reason="RTX PRO 6000 launch tuning requires its qualified hardware",
+)
+
+
+def inputs(prefix, queries, cache_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, kv_heads=2):
+    torch.manual_seed(78013 + prefix + queries)
+    q = torch.randn((queries, 32, 192), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k = torch.randn((queries, kv_heads, 192), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    v = torch.randn((queries, kv_heads, 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    kb = torch.randn((prefix, kv_heads, 192), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(
+        cache_dtype
+    )
+    vb = torch.randn((prefix, kv_heads, 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(
+        cache_dtype
+    )
+    qo = torch.tensor([0, queries], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    ki = torch.tensor([0, prefix], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices = torch.arange(prefix, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    return q, k, v, kb, vb, qo, ki, indices
+
+
+def execute(data, **kwargs):
+    q, k, v, kb, vb, qo, ki, indices = data
+    output = torch.empty((q.shape[0], 32, 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    kwargs.setdefault("extend_prefix_lens_cpu", [kb.shape[0]])
+    attention.extend_attention_fwd(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        output,
+        kb,
+        vb,
+        qo,
+        ki,
+        indices,
+        None,
+        True,
+        None,
+        q.shape[0],
+        1.0,
+        1.0,
+        sm_scale=192**-0.5,
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+    return output
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", [0, 257, 8191, 8192, 8193])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("queries", [512, 513])
+def test_mimo_global_fp8_tiles_match_original_kernel(monkeypatch, prefix, queries):
+    data = inputs(prefix, queries)
+    with monkeypatch.context() as original:
+        original.setattr(attention, "_is_rtx_pro_6000", False)
+        reference = execute(data)
+    result = execute(data)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.isfinite(result).all()
+    difference = result.float() - reference.float()
+    relative_rmse = (
+        difference.square().mean().sqrt() / reference.float().square().mean().sqrt()
+    )
+    assert relative_rmse.item() < 0.005
+    torch.testing.assert_close(result, reference, atol=0.002, rtol=0.02)
+    if prefix < 8192:
+        assert torch.equal(result, reference)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "kind", ["short", "bf16", "swa", "other-kv-heads", "missing-prefix-metadata"]
+)
+def test_other_attention_paths_keep_the_original_result(monkeypatch, kind):
+    data = inputs(
+        8192,
+        127 if kind == "short" else 513,
+        cache_dtype=torch.bfloat16 if kind == "bf16" else torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+        kv_heads=4 if kind == "other-kv-heads" else 2,
+    )
+    kwargs = {}
+    if kind == "swa":
+        kwargs = {
+            "sliding_window_size": 128,
+            "sinks": torch.linspace(-2, 2, 32, device="cuda"),
+        }
+    elif kind == "missing-prefix-metadata":
+        kwargs = {"extend_prefix_lens_cpu": None}
+    with monkeypatch.context() as original:
+        original.setattr(attention, "_is_rtx_pro_6000", False)
+        reference = execute(data, **kwargs)
+    result = execute(data, **kwargs)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(result, reference)
+
+
+def test_captured_prefill_keeps_original_tiles_for_shorter_replay(monkeypatch):
+    data = inputs(8192, 512)
+    with monkeypatch.context() as original:
+        original.setattr(attention, "_is_rtx_pro_6000", False)
+        reference = execute(data)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        captured = execute(data)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(captured, reference)
+
+    # Replay does not re-evaluate CPU prefix metadata. A graph must therefore
+    # retain the original reduction partition when its device lengths shrink.
+    data[6][1] = 257
+    with monkeypatch.context() as original:
+        original.setattr(attention, "_is_rtx_pro_6000", False)
+        reference = execute(data)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(captured, reference)
